title: Signal Nexus — Hedgehog Compact Playbook (Apr 2026)
body:
Objective:
Condense a week of frontline intake into a compact playbook for 2-week spikes. This doc surfaces recurrent customer asks tied to runtime behavior (kv-cache misses, cold-start latency, model-fallback quirks) and proposes low-risk probes + one midweight engineering spike.

Summary (topline):
- Source window: support tickets + partner calls + SRE alerts from 2026-04-01 → 2026-04-10.
- Signal themes: 1) KV cache churn causing repeated token re-computation in multi-turn chat; 2) unpredictable latency spikes for small-batch dedicated customers during autoscaling events; 3) confusion about model-fallback semantics when a preferred variant is unavailable.
- Net ask: pragmatic controls (tunable TTLs, per-route cache hints, fallback transparency) and 2 UX clarifications in Console + API docs.

Signal clusters (short):
1) KV-cache churn (high frequency, medium severity)
   - Representative: "Our customer sees a 3x token-cost jump on long chats overnight — looks like the system keeps dropping their prefix cache." (Account: FinScribe)
   - Triggers: frequent small restarts on dedicated nodes; many short new sessions from client-side; long-tail sequence lengths.
   - Fast probes: expose a per-route cache-stats endpoint (counts: hits/misses/evictions) + opt-in "sticky affinity" for routes with high reuse.
   - Impact estimate: medium token-cost savings for top 20% of affected customers; ops troubleshooting time cut.

2) Autoscale latency ripple (medium frequency, high severity for a subset)
   - Representative: "When we hit a burst, our p95 jumps to 800ms for 60s and our SLAs spike — reports happen during lunch windows." (SaaS analytics client)
   - Hypothesis: warmup + model-variant selection + load-balancing creates transient queuing; batching heuristics behave poorly under rapid node churn.
   - Fast probes: short-term mitigation = allow customers to pin a minimum instance count on Dedicated (soft reserve), or configurable scale cooldown.
   - Engineering spike: collect time-series traces across scale events to quantify queues + kernel-init time; run controlled blast tests.

3) Model-fallback opacity (low frequency, high customer friction)
   - Representative: "We got a different voice from the model mid-rolling deploy and couldn't tell why" (Large enterprise)
   - Problem: Console & API logs lack explicit reason codes (capacity / version mismatch / policy).
   - Quick fixes: add a per-request metadata field (fallback_reason) and a Console banner mapping common codes to remediation steps.

Representative snippets (raw intake):
- "why did the tokens jump?" (ticket #CS-9314)
- "p95 went sideways at 11:45 — we lost telemetry on 2 calls" (partner call notes)
- "fallback to smaller family without telling us caused hallucination variance" (account note)

Low-cost tactical actions (<= 2w):
- Add "cache-stats" debug header on response (hits/misses/last-evict-age) behind a feature flag. Owner: CS + SDK team. Ticket: JIRA-RW-4176.
- Console: Add "fallback history" timeline on request detail view (show variant switch events). Owner: product-console. PR reference: github.com/redwood/console/pull/1298 (sketch).
- Offer a customer-facing KB: "When tokens spike: troubleshooting checklist" (doc draft attached in linked_artifacts). Owner: CS docs.
- Launch an internal runbook for SRE on scale ripple diagnosis (playbook with trace queries + blast test checklist). Owner: SRE.

Medium-weight engineering proposals (2–6w):
- Per-route cache hints: allow upstream to specify expected session reuse patterns (ttl_hint: low/medium/high). Scheduler can use this to place warm affinity. Rough backlog ticket: JIRA-RW-4194. Expected dev cost: 3–4 sprints across runtime + routing layers.
- Autoscale cooldown and warm pool: implement configurable cooldown window + tiny warm pool for dedicated clusters to absorb spikes. Risk: marginal infra cost increase.

Open questions & risks (for leadership):
- Cost vs value: some customers want guaranteed warm capacity — do we price a minimal warm pool as an add-on or bake into Dedicated?
- Telemetry overhead: adding more per-request headers/metrics increases cardinality — need SRE buy-in on retention and sample rates.
- Backwards compatibility: exposing fallback_reason in responses may leak internal policy details; need to review security/contract.

Priority recommendation (short):
1) Ship debug cache header (feature-flagged) + KB within 2 weeks.
2) Expose fallback history in Console (scoped MVP).
3) Start an autoscale blast test and collect traces; decide on warm pool pricing after data.

Suggested owners & next steps (this week):
- Triage meeting: Mon 2026-04-19, 10:00 PT (attendees: CS triage, runtime eng lead, SRE lead, product-console PM).
- Quick tickets to open: JIRA-RW-4176 (cache-header), JIRA-RW-4177 (console-fallback-view), JIRA-RW-4181 (autoscale-trace-blast).
- CS-run: ready short customer comms for FinScribe and the analytics client explaining planned probes and offering temporary workarounds.

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep this compact — ops hates long playbooks in postmortem.
- Flag for legal: are we allowed to show variant reasons for EU customers? (privacy/regulatory check).
- Consider linking to recent "kv-cache-friction-notes" doc for cross-team context.

Appendix (quick raw data pointers):
- Sample ticket excerpts pulled into the ticket JIRA-RW-4176.
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-quirks (2026-04-05) — see pinned messages.
- Initial blast-test script sketch: /docs/runbooks/blast-autoscale.md (internal).

End (short) — feedback welcome: please comment inline on the console mock and suggest which accounts we pilot the warm-pool with.
